newsitem.title: USA: Northeastern US spot power firms on chill, outages.
newsitem.headline: Northeastern US spot power firms on chill, outages.

text.p: Day-ahead bulk electricity prices in the Northeast continued their rise Wednesday amid frigid temperatures and recent plant outages in the region.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Thursday delivery in the eastern half of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) firmed to $32.50-$33.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Tuesday's $32.00-$33.00 for delivery today.
Off-peak, non-firm power for day-ahead delivery in eastern NYPP widened to $22.00-$24.00 from Tuesday's quote of $24.00.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Thursday widened to $27.00-$29.00 from $26.00-$27.00 Tuesday.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Thursday held steady at $17.50-$18.50.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border was quoted again at $33.00-$35.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for day-ahead delivery at the NU border jumped to $28.00 from Tuesday's $24.00.
Northeastern skies are forecast to remain clear through Thursday night ahead of a storm system bringing snow showers late Friday into Saturday, clearing again Sunday.

Temperatures, in the meantime, are expected to average below normal through the weekend, with Wednesday averaging 12-18 degrees F below normal, then moderating to near normal to 5 degrees below normal Friday and Saturday before dropping back to 10-17 degrees below normal Sunday.

The 832 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick plant in Scriba, N.Y., resumed power production today after being taken off line last week to remove fish and debris accumulated on screens in water intakes that supply cooling water to the plant.

The two units at the Indian Point nuclear generating complex north of New York City remained shut. The 975 MW unit 2, which was shut January 18 to correct problems with a feedwater valve, will likely restart next week. The 965 MW unit 3 was expected to stay idled through mid-February for replacement work in its primary containment area.
Swing natural gas values at the New York City gate firmed to $3.70-$4.00 per million British thermal units from Tuesday's $3.60 mark.
